items.title: Vulnerabilities in Moxa Remote Connect Suite (MRC Client) and OnCell G3150A-LTE Series
items.summary: Classification: Important, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Not Defined, CVSSv3.1: 7.7, CVEs: CVE-2026-111459, CVE-2026-111460, CVE-2026-111461, Summary: This security advisory addresses one vulnerability identified in Moxa Remote Connect Suite (MRC Client) and two vulnerabilities identified in the OnCell G3150A-LTE Series. CVE-2026-111459 - Unauthenticated server-supplied OpenVPN configuration in Moxa Remote Connect Suite (MRC Client) An improper certificate validation vulnerability exists in Moxa Remote Connect Suite (MRC Client). Under certain conditions, an unauthenticated attacker with on-path access to the communication between the MRC Client and its server could impersonate a trusted server and conduct a man-in-the-middle attack, potentially compromising the confidentiality and integrity of communications. CVE-2026-111460 - Static HTTPS private key and CA private key in firmware in OnCell G3150A-LTE Series A hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability exists in the OnCell G3150A-LTE Series. Under certain conditions, an unauthenticated remote attacker could obtain shared cryptographic key material and use it to impersonate affected devices that have not regenerated their cryptographic keys, potentially compromising the confidentiality and integrity of management communications. CVE-2026-111461 - SMS upgrade argument reaches system() unescaped in OnCell G3150A-LTE Series An OS command injection vulnerability exists in OnCell G3150A-LTE Series. When the SMS management functionality is enabled and configured, a remote attacker with the required privileges could exploit insufficient input validation in the SMS management functionality to execute arbitrary commands on the affected device. Moxa has developed appropriate solutions to address the vulnerability.

items.title: Japanese virtual desktop cloud hacked so hard it asks to be banned
items.summary: Japanese ISP GMO Internet has warned customers the cloudy desktop service it offers as an ideal foreign exchange trading environment was compromised by an attacker, and that it had been slow to improve the service's security. GMO runs a service called Onamae.com Desktop Cloud and last week admitted “a third party had installed malicious programs in the server environments of some customers.” That’s never welcome news but is an especially poor outcome because the servers host cloudy Windows desktops that GMO recommends customers use to host foreign exchange trading applications. In later updates the company revealed that some customers reported “unauthorized operations were performed on their trading accounts” and advised that third parties had probably seen users’ passwords for trading services. The next day, the company advised users to immediately change passwords for their trading accounts, and to do so using a device that they don’t use for trading. The company has since admitted that its Onamae.com Desktop Cloud service’s “systems had security vulnerabilities, that its environment was accessed without authorization, and that customer information was taken outside the Company.” “Some customers have also reported transactions in their trading accounts that they do not recognize.” Those transactions have GMO sufficiently worried that it contacted major trading services, asked them to forcibly terminate all active sessions, monitor for unauthorized transactions, and to block trade requests coming from the

items.title: 26 Oct 2026 Updated PHP Windows builds for Brotli security fix
items.summary: Classification: Critical, Solution: Official Fix, Exploit Maturity: Proof-of-Concept, CVSSv3.1: 9.2, CVEs: CVE-2026-111497, Summary: The PHP team announces updated Windows builds: PHP 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1. These builds include Brotli 1.2.1, which fixes CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in Brotli decompression. In PHP Windows builds, the vulnerable decoder can be reached through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled. This is disabled by default in cURL, but applications and HTTP client libraries can enable it. The -1 suffix identifies a Windows package rebuild with updated dependencies. These builds use the same PHP source releases, and the PHP runtime versions remain unchanged. The updated packages are available on the downloads page.

items.title: Attack on email hosting provider for German far right party AfD exposed 345k accounts
items.summary: The cyberattack on Alternative for Germany (AfD), the country’s most prominent far-right political party, exposed hundreds of thousands of confidential emails and attachments, as well as more than 345,000 unique email addresses. Have I Been Pwned confirmed the scale of the breach for the first time today, after AfD officially disclosed the September attack on its hosting provider last week. AfD said in its statement that “only a few email accounts were illegally copied,” but admitted a large amount of the data was taken from them, resulting in an extensive data breach.

items.title: Energy giant ENGIE discloses data breach affecting customers
items.summary: French energy giant ENGIE, one of the world's largest power and natural gas providers, confirmed that attackers stole customer data after breaching a marketing platform used by business partners. ENGIE operates in renewable energy, infrastructure, and customer energy supply in 30 countries, employs over 90,000 people, and reported €71.9 billion in revenue last year. An ENGIE spokesperson told BleepingComputer that it cut off the attackers' access to the compromised platform and that they didn't breach the company's internal systems.

items.title: Moscow faces internet disruptions as foreign leaders gather for summits
items.summary: Russia warned that mobile internet access in central Moscow could be disrupted this week as authorities tighten security ahead of two international summits expected to draw foreign leaders to the capital. The restrictions will be in place from October 27 to 29, coinciding with the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit and the Russia-Africa summit, Russia's Ministry of Digital Development said Monday. Voice calls, Wi-Fi networks and websites on a government-approved list will remain accessible during the disruptions, the ministry said. The list, known as the internet "whitelist," includes government websites, Russian social media platforms, banks and online marketplaces. Introduced in 2025 amid widespread mobile internet shutdowns, the system allows users to access selected services while much of the wider internet remains unavailable. The restrictions come as Moscow prepares to host senior officials from several countries, including the presidents of Iran and Equatorial Guinea, the emir of Qatar, the chairman of Libya's Presidential Council and Venezuela's vice president, who are expected to attend the gas exporters' summit.

items.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
items.summary: Highway thieves are using sophisticated digital tactics that investigators worry make it easy to rob trucks carrying millions in expensive data center equipment. NBC News spoke to “several industry leaders, consultants, and investigators advising law enforcement” offices probing the biggest thefts yet and reported that since June, thieves have “made away with more than $100 million in data center freight.” Here’s how they said thieves get away with it: First, thieves hack freight brokers’ accounts on shipment-listing websites and post fake shipments to lure real bids, then send a malicious link to any trucking companies that respond. Once victims click, thieves install software to take control of their accounts and start bidding on real shipments. Sometimes, a real delivery driver is hired to collect the cargo, unaware of the scam, and other times fake driver’s licenses are used to get accomplices hired. Either way, the goods are eventually transferred to a driver working with the thieves to resell the gear, and, in one of the largest thefts, tracking coordinates were spoofed to prevent digital monitoring. Equipment commonly targeted includes “servers, fiber-optic cables, computer memory chips, copper wires, and bitcoin mining machines,” NBC News reported.

items.title: Suomen kriittisissä verkoissa tapahtui jotain outoa – Fakta­baari: Toiminnan takana vakoilu­­ohjelmiin kytketty yhtiö
items.summary: Israelilaisen mainosyhtiön epäilyttävä mainoskampanja ulottui Suomessa sairaaloiden, viranomaisten ja muiden yhteiskunnalle kriittisten toimijoiden tietoverkkoihin, kertoo Faktabaari. Tietoturvayhtiö Confiantilta peräisin olevan aineiston mukaan israelilaisen Discover-Tech-yhtiön mainoksia näytettiin Suomessa touko–heinäkuussa tuhansia kertoja. Niitä näkyi noin kymmenessä eri verkossa, joihin liittyvien internetosoitteiden joukossa oli muun muassa sairaaloiden, poliisin, ulkoministeriön, pankkien ja energiayhtiöiden osoitteita. Valtaosa mainoksista näkyi Android-laitteilla. Kampanjan tilaajaa ei tunneta. Toronton yliopiston Citizen Lab -tutkimusryhmä ja tietoturvayhtiö Confiant paljastivat lokakuussa, että Discover-Techin mainoksia voitiin käyttää vakoiluohjelmien levittämiseen. Mainokset näyttivät tavallisilta, mutta niiden sisällä oli piilokoodia. Koodi pystyi tarkistamaan, oliko mainoksen nähnyt laite valittu vakoilun kohteeksi. Jos oli, laitteeseen voitiin yrittää asentaa vakoiluohjelma käyttäjän huomaamatta. Mainosten kautta kerättyjä tietoja voidaan käyttää ihmisten tunnistamiseen ja myöhempien vakoiluiskujen valmisteluun. Mainosten kautta tapahtuva hyökkäys perustuu zero-click-periaatteeseen, jossa asennus tapahtuu automaattisesti. Käyttäjää ei siis tarvitse erehdyttää tekemään virhettä. Citizen Labin tutkijat vahvistivat, että näin oli tartutettu vakoiluohjelmia Al Jazeera -uutiskanavan työntekijöiden laitteisiin. Maailmanlaajuisesti Discover-Techin mainoksia näkyi yli 70 000 sovelluksessa ja 120 000 verkkosivustolla. Suomesta ei ole näyttöä vakoiluohjelmatartunnoista. Mainoksen näkyminen tietyn organisaation verkossa ei todista, että juuri sen työntekijöitä olisi yritetty vakoilla.

Suomesta ei ole näyttöä vakoiluohjelmatartunnoista. Mainoksen näkyminen tietyn organisaation verkossa ei todista, että juuri sen työntekijöitä olisi yritetty vakoilla.

items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog (PHP)
items.summary: CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and updated the PHP Alert, Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching: CVE-2026-109618 – PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability CVE-2026-109619 – PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.
items.summary_html:
CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and updated the PHP Alert, Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching:  

CVE-2026-109618 – PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability 
CVE-2026-109619 – PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability 

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.
